title.narrative: Responding to flooding in El Salvador as a result of the Central American Gyre

description.narrative: After the strong and continuous rainfall recorded from 15 to 21 June in the Salvadoran territory, influenced by tropical storm Alberto, located in the Gulf of Mexico, by the Central American Monsoon Gyre and the pressure zone of the Intertropical Convergence Line, the central government activated the emergency systems by issuing a State of National Emergency decree on 16 June for 15 days from that date through the Legislative Assembly. The central government activated the emergency systems by issuing on 16 June the decree of National State of Emergency for 15 days from that date through the Legislative Assembly; the suspension of classes in public and private educational centres for two days; and the Legislative Assembly declared a national holiday for the public and private sector on 18 June. -Cash transfers: It is proposed to make cash transfers to families in the affected communities in the amount of $75 (52% of the total amount of the MEB), this amount has been calculated based on budget availability respecting the guidelines established in relation to the Basic Food Basket $131.95 in El Salvador. Through a single transfer, beneficiary families will be able to access resources to cover their basic needs, such as food, hygiene supplies, medicines, transport, agricultural inputs and other elements they consider essential. This intervention seeks to alleviate the impact on food insecurity caused by the meteorological phenomena described above. In addition, it will build on the practice already in place in Caritas El Salvador with regard to the management of transfers.
